children: to drain surplus liquidity Our Bureau Mumbai|Kolkata: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has raised the minimum daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance requirement for scheduled banks to 99% from 90%, effective from mid-October. The move is aimed at draining surplus liquidity in the banking system as the central bank shifts towards calibrated tightening amid a liquidity surplus of about 4 lakh crore.

In a notification on Friday, the RBI said banks will have to maintain a minimum daily balance of 99% of the CRR requirement from the fortnight beginning October 16. CRR is the amount of deposits banks maintain with the RBI without earning interest. The ratio currently stands at 3%, which means that out of every 100 of deposits, a bank has to keep 3 with the RBI without earning interest.

So far, banks have had the operational flexibility to maintain only 90% of the required amount without attracting penal action. "On a review of the current liquidity conditions, it has been decided to increase the minimum daily maintenance of the CRR from 90% of the requirement to 99% effective from the fortnight beginning October 16, 2026," the RBI said.

Bankers said the new measure will curtail operational freedom. "So far, in a fortnight, banks had the flexibility to maintain 90% of the required CRR amount for seven days and maintain 110% for the next half of the reporting fortnight so that the average comes out to 100%. That flexibility will now go as banks will mostly have to maintain 100% at all times.

Other than some operational changes, this new norm will not lead to any major changes for banks," said Gopal Tripathi, head-treasury and capital markets at Jana Small Finance Bank. The central bank has decided to raise the daily requirement instead of tinkering with the CRR rate, which, according to RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra's post-policy comments, is "the least preferred" tool. "RBI had offered CRR exemptions on FCNR (B) deposit inflows through the dedicated foreign currency mobilisation programme, and therefore any hike in the CRR would not drain the additional flows," said a treasury executive, who did not wish to be identified.

title: RBI Raises Minimum CRR Maintenance Requirement to 99%
